disclosure.en: Robo-Kit is an educational tool, not a registered advisor or dealer in Canada or the US. It does not know your full situation and does not tell you what to buy. Figures come from Robo-Kit's code and public data; results are hypothetical and not guarantees. You make your own decisions.

projection_disclosure.en: The projections are hypothetical in nature, do not reflect actual investment results and are not guarantees of future results. They come from re-sampling past monthly returns, re-centred on published planning assumptions after fund fees. Results may vary with each use and over time. Other investments not considered may have characteristics similar or superior to those analysed.

About how much will you invest to start?
Roughly what share of all your savings and investments is this?

questions.text: Over one year, which range of results would you be most comfortable with?
Imagine the market falls sharply and in three months your {amount} is worth {after}. What would you most likely do?
Over ten years, which would you rather have?
When you invest, which worries you more?
When interest rates go up, what usually happens to the price of existing bonds?
A fund that promises 2x the daily move of an index is held for a whole year. Will it return exactly 2x the index's yearly return?

options.text: No, it can be quite different

en.definition: A basket of many investments you buy and sell like one share on a stock exchange.
A fund that copies a market index, such as the S&P 500, instead of picking investments.
The yearly fee a fund takes, as a percentage of what you hold. 0.20% is $20 a year per $10,000.
How much the value swings up and down. Higher volatility means bigger ups and bigger downs.
How far the value fell from its previous high before recovering.
Spreading money across many investments so one bad result hurts less.
A family of investments that behave alike: stocks, bonds, cash, real estate, gold.
A loan to a government or company that pays interest and returns the money at a set date.
When interest rates rise, existing bonds lose value, because new bonds pay more. Longer bonds move more.
Roughly how much a bond fund's price moves when rates change by one point. Duration 7 means about 7%.
The income an investment pays each year, as a percentage of its price.
The fund removes most of the effect of exchange-rate swings, for a small cost.
Funds that try to return 2x, 3x or -1x an index's move for one day. Held longer, results can differ a lot from 2x the index.
Trading back to your target mix after markets have moved it.
How much ups and downs you are willing to live with.
How much loss your situation can absorb: time until you need the money, savings cushion, income.
The return each fund would need for today's market mix to be a sensible holding. Robo-Kit uses it instead of past returns, which are too noisy.
Re-running the calculation on thousands of reshuffled histories and averaging, so one lucky period does not decide the mix.
How much two investments move together, from -1 (opposite) to +1 (in lockstep).
Return above cash per unit of volatility. Higher is better, all else equal.
How far a portfolio's returns tend to stray from a reference portfolio's, per year.
The gap between the price buyers offer and sellers ask. Thinly traded funds have wider gaps.
How much money a fund holds in total. Very small funds are more likely to close.
A fund that sells options on its holdings for extra income, giving up part of the upside.
A company that owns and rents out property, such as apartments, offices or warehouses.
Countries whose economies and markets are still developing, such as China, India and Brazil.
The general rise in prices, which shrinks what each dollar buys.
A fund holding very short government bills or bank deposits. It barely moves and pays about the short-term interest rate.
Tax-sheltered accounts. A TFSA shelters growth from tax; an RRSP gives a deduction now and taxes withdrawals. A tax professional can say which fits you.
A method that starts from the market's own implied returns and blends in a view only as much as you trust it.
A result the rules would have produced on past data. No one actually earned it.

flags.label: Expected US stock-market volatility (VIX)
flags.evidence: A high VIX means big expected swings. In research, periods of high fear have on average been followed by higher, not lower, returns. Context only; it does not change the portfolio.

flags.label: Geopolitical risk index (Caldara-Iacoviello)
flags.evidence: Counts newspaper coverage of wars, threats and terrorism. High readings have hit prices on impact, but they have not reliably predicted returns. Context and stress scenarios only.

flags.label: US economic policy uncertainty
flags.evidence: Measures newspaper coverage of policy uncertainty. In research, higher readings have on average come before higher stock returns (a risk premium). Context only.

flags.label: Canada economic policy uncertainty
flags.evidence: Same measure for Canada. Context only.

flags.label: US high-yield credit spread
flags.evidence: The extra yield riskier companies pay. Wide spreads mean lenders are nervous. Context only.

flags.label: Bank of Canada policy rate
flags.evidence: The rate the Bank of Canada targets. It sets what cash and short-term savings pay.

flags.label: Canada inflation (CPI, year over year)
flags.evidence: How fast prices are rising. The Bank of Canada targets 2%.

flags.label: US yield curve (10-year minus 3-month)
flags.evidence: An inverted curve has often come before recessions, with long and variable lags. It is not a timing signal. Context only.

flags.label: Canada yield curve (10-year minus 3-month)
flags.evidence: An inverted curve has often come before recessions, with long and variable lags. It is not a timing signal. Context only.

flags.label: US dollar in Canadian dollars
flags.reading: the US dollar is up 1.8% over 12 months
flags.evidence: When the US dollar rises, unhedged US funds held in Canadian dollars gain from it, and the reverse. Context only.
